title: VariantSelection
description: The variants an engine has selected for one interaction, with the report of how they were chosen (spec.md §3.9). This is the document 'consumer-session/variants' returns: the sample, not the whole space. The space itself is the shape language's variant-space document (design 2.2).

variants.description: In run order: the base variant first, then pins, then covering variants (spec.md §4.3).

Variant.title: Variant
Variant.description: One variant. The assignment is the identity; the id is derived from it (spec.md §2.2).

id.description: 'base', or the ';'-joined '<dimension-id>=<point>' renderings of the dimensions that differ from their default, in variant-space order.

assignment.description: One point per active dimension, in variant-space order. Inactive dimensions are absent, never null.

label.description: Display only: the id with dimension ids shortened to the shortest unique trailing path segments. Never recorded in a pact file, never accepted where an id is expected (spec.md §2.2).

origin.description: Why this variant is in the selection.

states.description: The interaction's provider states with this variant's parameters resolved (spec.md §6.4). The state document is design 2.5's.

Point.title: Point
Point.description: A dimension bound to one of its points.

SelectionReport.title: SelectionReport
SelectionReport.description: How the selection was chosen. Coverage figures are computed, never asserted (spec.md §3.3).

strategy.description: The strategy actually applied, after 'auto' resolved (spec.md §3.2).

algorithm.description: The named selection algorithm (spec.md §3.7). A different algorithm is a different name, never a redefinition.

selected.description: Number of variants in the selection; at least 1, because the base variant is unconditional.

boundaries.description: Whether the minimal and maximal variants were seeded (spec.md §3.1).

exclusions.description: The exclusions in force, each with the reason it carries and what it removed (spec.md §3.5).

notes.description: Anything the selection needs to say for itself — a dropped target, a saturated count, a waiver.

size.description: Variants in the space, counted per spec.md §2.3. When 'exact' is false this is the saturation bound, meaning 'at least this many'.

exact.description: False when counting saturated against the largest budget in force.

targets.description: Reachable coverage targets at this strength, after exclusions (spec.md §3.3).

removed.description: Targets removed because an exclusion makes them unreachable.

dropped.description: Reachable targets the sampler could not complete without matching an exclusion; reported rather than searched for (spec.md §3.5).

removed.description: Coverage targets this exclusion made unreachable.

code.description: Open vocabulary; unknown codes are displayed, never dispatched on.

target.description: For 'target-dropped': the target that was not covered.
